card.title: Your eyes can change what you hear

body.claim: What you see a mouth doing can change the sound you hear.
body.why: The McGurk effect is a perceptual phenomenon that demonstrates an interaction between hearing and vision in speech perception. When the syllables /ba-ba/ are spoken over the lip movements of /ga-ga/, the perception is of /da-da/. The effect is very robust: knowledge about it seems to have little effect on one's perception of it.

probes.question: The syllables /ba-ba/ are spoken over the lip movements of /ga-ga/. What do people typically perceive?
True or false: once you know about the McGurk effect, it stops working on you.

claims.claim: Title/claim: what you see a mouth doing can change the sound you hear
claims.quote: The illusion occurs when the auditory component of one sound is paired with the visual component of another sound, leading to the perception of a third sound.
